_comment: Registry of the kernel's automated tasks. Single source of truth for chat-agent delegation + cron reference. This installation's own tasks (and any field it overrides on a kernel task) live in agent/local/tasks.json, same shape; every reader sees the two merged by lib/registry.cjs (`node lib/registry.cjs tasks`). Edit, then run 'edva doctor' to verify cron + playbook alignment.

tasks.name: morning-digest
tasks.description: Compile calendar, tasks, news headlines, and weather; send to Edva.

tasks.name: context-sync
tasks.description: Re-index Apple Notes, iMessage, email memories, and project files into the context search database.

tasks.name: skill-repair
tasks.schedule_human: On demand the moment a repair is queued; hourly at :47 as a safety net
tasks.description: Same-day repair of a read-only browser action or page parser that stopped reading its site (queued by an installation's ingest job on a source's first bad run and by skill-health on the first failure day; lib/skill-repair.mjs). Reads the live page, rewrites the one action with the same output shape, verifies rows return, lands via self-improve-auto-apply. Silent. Queue: bin/skill-repair list. See ops-agent/jobs/skill-repair.md.

tasks.name: hum
tasks.schedule_human: Every 20 minutes — the always-on hum of ambient awareness
tasks.description: Every 20 minutes, evaluates the user's current situation (location, calendar, messages, git commits, audio context, weather) and decides whether to surface useful information, ask a context-building question, or stay silent. Most ticks exit silently via bash gates. Questions with answers grow memory files under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/ for better future context. Replaces the old lane-rotation pulse.

tasks.name: hum-review
tasks.description: Weekly self-assessment of hum: analyzes 7 days of ticks, pings, questions, answers, reactions, and memory growth. Emails the user a memo with engagement stats and proposed tuning. Never applies tuning automatically — proposals only. Read-only on all hum state files.

tasks.name: hum-consolidate
tasks.description: Nightly fold of the day's replies-to-hum-pings (hum-responses.jsonl) into the general wiki, so hum stops re-asking things the user already answered. Durable preferences/facts become linked, deduped wiki pages via wiki save; transient resolutions are skipped. Trigger gates on un-consolidated rows; silent (no email/ping/push). Replaced hum-answer's old realtime subsection routing (2026-06-28).

tasks.name: hum-daily
tasks.description: Chronicle of the last 24h of hum ticks — what harvesters discovered, what pings/questions were sent and why. Email (personal, starred) + short phone pointer. Direct script, no agent turn (bin/hum-daily-run, 2026-10-04).

tasks.name: hum-ideation
tasks.schedule_human: 4× daily at 6:00 AM, 11:00 AM, 2:00 PM, 7:00 PM local
tasks.description: Twice-daily proactive idea generation for hum. Reads calendar, tasks, gmail, trip-history, recent reactions. Builds a reinforcement-biased mix (exploit top categories, explore untested, retry failed with variation). Writes 8-15 new ideas to hum-ideas.jsonl + rebuilds the reaction scorecard. Never pings, never emails — ideas surface through the normal hum tick via the `ideas` harvester.

tasks.name: nightly-review
tasks.schedule_human: Weekly Tuesday at 5:00 AM — after the 4:00 AM daily summary it reads, moved from 3:00 AM on 2026-10-22 (launchd agent ai.claude.improvement-review, NOT cron — cron can't reach the in-session Max keychain; also runs on ephemeral Opus 5, not the webhook-dispatched ops supervisor, since 2026-07-28)
tasks.description: Weekly holistic system self-assessment and improvement memo, covering the prior 7 days. Job/script names retain the historical 'nightly-review' label. Chains improvement-plan on a clean exit.

tasks.name: improvement-plan
tasks.schedule_human: Chained by nightly-review on a clean exit; launchd agent ai.claude.improvement-plan (Tue 10:30 AM, past the review's 05:00 start plus both runs' caps) is a safety-net slot only, guarded against re-running on a stale report
tasks.description: Acts on every ACTION ITEM of the weekly Self Improvement Review: safe changes land on their own through self-improve-auto-apply (green check in Improvements), complex or high-blast-radius ones become Face-ID cards (rubric schema v4, 2026-09-29), questions go to the next review. Runs on ephemeral Opus 5 via run-ephemeral-opus.sh. Cards capped at 5 unsigned total.

tasks.name: wiki-audit
tasks.description: Nightly re-evaluation of the wiki pinned-page subset. Reads `data/wiki-access.jsonl` (last 7 days, MCP caller only), pins any unpinned page hit ≥ 5 times, unpins any pinned page with 0 hits AND pinned for ≥ 7 days AND not pin_locked. Logs the moves to the Improvements channel (green-check row) only when something changes (silent on no-op nights); no email since 2026-10-07. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API.

tasks.name: memory-snapshot
tasks.description: Auto-commit + push the auto-memory dir to its private backup repo. Idempotent on no-changes. Primary backup layer — protects against rm/corruption/bad-merge of the 80+ .md files at ~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/memory/. Pre-reindex tarballs in data/memory-snapshots/ are belt-and-suspenders.

tasks.name: wiki-db-snapshot
tasks.description: Hourly hot snapshot of data/memory-index.db via SQLite VACUUM INTO. Rotates to the last 24 copies under data/memory-db-snapshots/. Defense-in-depth backup for the wiki layer (`pages` / `page_links` / `page_revisions` / `pages_fts` and the legacy `memory_chunks` index) — protects against DB corruption (e.g. the 2026-05-02 FTS5 incident). Restore = `cp memory-db-snapshots/memory-index-<ts>.db data/memory-index.db`. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API.

tasks.name: wiki-cloud-sync
tasks.description: Off-box copy of the wiki. Reconciles Supabase wiki_pages / wiki_page_links / wiki_page_revisions (edva project) to data/memory-index.db via `bin/wiki-cloud-sync push` — stateless row-hash diff for pages+links, rowid cursor for revisions (data/wiki-cloud-sync.json). Pages 3 failures in a row via edva-notify --channel system. Restore = `wiki-cloud-sync restore --db <new-file>` then swap in + re-run wiki-embed. Check = `wiki-cloud-sync verify`. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API.

tasks.name: chrome-cdp-watch
tasks.description: Probe Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9222 and notify the user once per UP→DOWN transition so they can investigate a lost TCC grant / closed Chrome / chrome-devtools-mcp re-sign. Silent on recovery. Quiet hours 00:00–09:00 local defer the ping to the 09:00-tick. State in data/chrome-cdp-state.json. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API.

tasks.name: hum-explore
tasks.schedule_human: Daily at 12:30 PM and 5:30 PM local (clock-jobs.json); sends at most 2 a week
tasks.description: Hum exploration (replaced the weekly canary 2026-10-07): at most twice a week, 48h apart, sends the best fresh held-back discretionary item in a lane where hum is still guessing, as an ordinary 'Borderline pick:' ping through hum-ping (budget/dedup refusals apply), with one line on what it is and why it was sent, and the item's link. The user's reaction calibrates the lane via hum-engagement. Direct script, no agent turn: since 2026-10-15 the cron trigger kicks launchd agent ai.claude.hum-explore, whose run-hum-explore.sh checks the Max login (so the resolve-first gate and precheck can run) and then runs bin/hum-explore-run; no verified login means the pick is held.

tasks.name: usage-push
tasks.description: Push per-day model-weighted Claude usage/cost rollups (from edva-cost-report --push, unioning the ops/-light/-haiku ledgers) to the hosted /usage telemetry endpoint for central, durable monitoring across hosts. Sends the real metered weighted cost, not the SDK phantom estimate. Runs after midnight over a 2-day window; idempotent per (host, day). Requires EDVA_USAGE_TOKEN (or STATS_TOKEN) in .env. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API. Non-fatal when there are no cost rows. NOTE: confirm the cron slot via edva-cron-slots on the host.

tasks.name: recall-events-embed
tasks.description: Backfill local Ollama (nomic-embed-text) embeddings for high-value events in the events_fts recall index, powering recall_events mode:hybrid. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API. Degrades gracefully (recall stays FTS-only if Ollama is down). Added 2026-07-08 with the semantic-recall feature.

tasks.name: wiki-embed
tasks.description: Backfill local Ollama (nomic-embed-text) embeddings for new/changed wiki pages (pages -> page_embeddings in memory-index.db), powering wiki_search mode:hybrid. Re-embeds a page when its body_hash changes; prunes embeddings for deleted pages. Direct script — no webhook, no Anthropic API. Degrades gracefully (wiki_search stays FTS-only if Ollama is down). Added 2026-07-19 to extend hybrid recall from the event log to the curated wiki.

tasks.name: wiki-assoc
tasks.schedule_human: Daily 4:20 AM local (after wiki-embed); the model half runs in the launchd agent ai.claude.wiki-assoc-llm it kicks
tasks.description: Nightly writers for associative memory (system/wiki-architecture.md § Associative recall). Under cron, no model: `wiki-assoc nightly` folds new auto-recall judge rows into page_coactivation (pages kept together for the same message, decayed Hebbian weights), writes data/wiki-link-candidates.json (strong co-used pairs with no link, read by wiki-link-weave Step 5.5), and rebuilds page_activation (ACT-R base-level activation from judge-kept recalls and deliberate wiki_read/episode_get reads, never search hits). Then it kicks the on-demand launchd agent ai.claude.wiki-assoc-llm (run-wiki-assoc-llm.sh, behind max-auth-guard): typed fact extraction into page_facts and trigger cues into page_cues, each through the local → Sonnet ladder with a verbatim-evidence check and a per-run Sonnet cap. Silent; log agent/logs/wiki-assoc.log. Added 2026-10-24.

tasks.name: system-issue-review
tasks.schedule_human: Daily at 4:27 AM local (launchd agent ai.claude.system-issue-review, NOT cron — cron can't reach the in-session Max keychain; also runs on ephemeral Opus 5, not the webhook-dispatched ops supervisor, since 2026-07-28)
phrases: why does that alert keep firing
tasks.description: Nightly root-cause pass over Edva's own system channel. Clusters the last 14 days of alerts into distinct issues (by condition, not wording), correlates recovery messages, closes out verified fixes, then works two lanes: up to 3 fix attempts and up to 3 cheaper review-only passes. Every issue is reviewed even if it healed itself (2026-07-25) -- a recovery closes the incident, never the issue, and nothing reaches a terminal status without a recorded root cause. Low/moderate fixes are implemented + critic-reviewed + committed autonomously and shown as a green-check card in the Improvements channel; high-risk fixes are staged as one Face-ID card per night. A review concluding no code change is warranted is recorded silently (status reviewed / resolution reviewed-no-fix) and surfaces in the weekly nightly-review roundup.

tasks.name: system-issue-review-critical
tasks.schedule_human: Hourly at :52 (--critical-only; dispatches only on a NEW critical alert). launchd agent ai.claude.system-issue-review-critical, NOT cron — cron can't reach the in-session Max keychain; also runs on ephemeral Opus 5, not the webhook-dispatched ops supervisor, since 2026-07-28
tasks.description: Same-day escalation lane for system-issue-review, added 2026-07-25 so a capability-down issue does not wait up to 24h for the nightly pass. Runs hourly but dispatches ONLY when a genuinely new critical-marker alert landed in the system channel; warnings, recoveries, and repeats of an issue already in flight all wait for the nightly run. Deduplication lives in lib/system-issue-gate.mjs and is the whole point: in a real 14-day window most critical alerts were repeats of one or two conditions, so a naive gate would have fired over a dozen heavy dispatches in one night for one already-carded issue (heavy tier = the ops supervisor, which runs claude-sonnet-5; an escalation turn is one of the most expensive turns it runs). When it does dispatch, the job scopes to a single cluster on a ~15-minute budget.

tasks.name: cost-efficiency-review
tasks.schedule_human: Daily at 2:37 AM local (launchd agent ai.claude.cost-efficiency-review, NOT cron — cron can't reach the in-session Max keychain; runs on ephemeral Opus 5 like the rest of the improvement family). Slot reserved via edva-cron-slots.
phrases: why is edva using so much budget
how much did edva cost today
tasks.description: Daily review of WHERE the Max budget actually went in the last 24h — not which job spent the most, but whether the spend bought WORK or bought CONTEXT. Reads a pre-fetched `edva-cost-report --efficiency --json` (the trigger fetches it un-sandboxed) and compares against the 2026-08-06 baseline: cost split by token type, the measured context FLOOR per supervisor, the working window above it, and the compact/rotate churn that follows when that window closes. Flags a regression when overhead rises >5 points, a floor grows >5k, a working window drops under 40k, or 24h spend exceeds 1.4x the 7d median — then attributes it to a specific change (a new always-loaded CLAUDE.md section, an added MCP server, a gate that stopped gating, a job that got heavier) and files cuts through the unified self-improvement pipeline: low/moderate auto-apply with a green-check card, high risk (model tier, output quality, capability removal) as a Face-ID card it can never self-approve. Silent when nothing regressed. Exists because a single day can burn a large share of the weekly cap, most of it cache traffic, and nightly-review's weekly job-shaped cost lens could not see it.

tasks.name: inbox-mem-sync
tasks.description: Pull recent mail into the inbox memory channel (FTS + embeddings in memory-index.db) so `recall` — and the release freshness gate that asks it — can see what the mailbox already knows. Silent; no user output.

tasks.name: inbox-mem-sync-deep
tasks.description: Nightly wide-window inbox re-index + prune. Repairs whatever the 20-minute short window missed (outage, burst past --max) and bounds index growth at 120 days.
